edge.title: Swap Muon for NorMuon (per-row/col 2nd-moment norm), lr 0.025→0.035
edge.summary: Hidden matrices switch from Muon to NorMuon: after Nesterov momentum, 12 NS iterations and the max(1,m/n)^0.5 scale, an EMA (β2=0.95) of the mean squared update along the longer axis (per row; per column for the wide mlp.proj) rescales the update by 1/√EMA, which is then rescaled back to its original Frobenius norm. This evens out update RMS across neurons while keeping Muon's overall step size; decoupled WD stays at 0.025 and the lr rises 0.025→0.035. train_steps drops 3375→3300 and the result is claimed at the step-3250 validation, 50 steps before the LR reaches 0.

changes.label: NorMuon optimizer for hidden matrices
changes.detail: New normuon_update/NorMuon: Muon's momentum→NS→aspect scale, then second_momentum (fp32, (m,1) if m≥n else (1,n)) lerps toward mean(u²) with 1−0.95 (hard-coded), u *= rsqrt(clamp(v,1e-10)) in bf16, and u is rescaled to its pre-normalization Frobenius norm; WD and lr applied as in Muon.

changes.label: Hidden lr 0.025 → 0.035
changes.detail: optimizer2 = NorMuon(..., lr=0.035, weight_decay=0.025); aux AdamW and init unchanged.

changes.label: train_steps 3375 → 3300, claim 3250
changes.detail: The linear cooldown (frac 0.7) now ends at 3300; the claimed 3250 is a regular 125-step validation reached with the LR at ≈2% of peak.

changes.label: Loader/init cosmetics, dead Muon class
changes.detail: distributed_data_generator calls dist.get_world_size()/get_rank() inline, init uses a w = p.data alias, and the original Muon class stays in the file unused.

edge.parent_check: consistent — nearest-code is #6: same num_trials harness, #6 normal init and aux AdamW; only the hidden optimizer class, its lr and train_steps change.
edge.noise: Inline dist.get_world_size()/get_rank() in the data generator, a w = p.data alias in init, and the unused Muon class left in place.

techniques.note: core path: Nesterov mu=0.95 → 12 NS iters → max(1,m/n)^0.5; decoupled WD 0.025
EMA(β2 0.95) of mean u² along longer axis → u·rsqrt(EMA), Frobenius norm restored; lr 0.035
AdamW embed 0.3 / head 1/320 / 1-D 0.01, betas (0.8, 0.95), eps 1e-10, wd 0
flat for 30%, then linear to 0 at step 3300 (cooldown_frac 0.7)
train_steps 3300, claimed at the step-3250 eval (LR ≈2% of peak)
proj weights (attn/mlp/lm head) zero; others N(0, 0.33/fan_in); all biases 0

hparams.normuon.axis: per row if m >= n (q/k/v/attn.proj/mlp.fc), per column for wide mlp.proj

mechanisms.name: NorMuon second-moment normalization
mechanisms.explain: normuon_update runs the usual Muon pipeline, then averages u² over the shorter axis (one value per row for q/k/v/attn.proj/mlp.fc, per column for the wide mlp.proj), lerps an fp32 buffer toward it with weight 0.05 (β2=0.95, no bias correction) and multiplies u by rsqrt(max(v, 1e-10)). The result is rescaled to the pre-normalization Frobenius norm, so the global step size stays Muon's (lr·max(1,m/n)^0.5·‖NS‖) and only the relative per-neuron magnitudes change; decoupled WD lr·0.025 is applied before the step as in Muon.

caveats: Despite the 'full NorMuon' vs 'NorMuon-lite' naming, this normalizer is numerically identical to #9's NorMuon-lite (same shape-dependent axis, β2 0.95, clamp 1e-10, Frobenius restore, no bias correction); #9 and #10 differ in WD (0.025 here vs none + u/w floor), lr, init and steps. For the wide mlp.proj (768×3072) the statistic is per input column, not per output neuron. The table's 'end 50 steps early' matches train_steps 3300 vs the 3250 claim.
